transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi doctor. I'm here because I've been struggling a lot with focusing and paying attention to my tasks lately. It's just really hard for me to stay focused on what I'm doing for more than a few minutes.
Do you also experience restlessness, fidgeting, or an inability to stay still, especially in quiet or low-stimulation environments?
No, I don't really have those issues with fidgeting or staying still. My struggles are much more about losing my focus and getting easily distracted by other things.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with focus and distraction, and did they start when you were a child or did they develop more recently?
I’ve been dealing with these specific difficulties for about two years and three months now. However, these focus issues actually started way back when I was a kid, definitely before I turned 12.
How do these focus and distraction issues affect your daily life, such as your work, relationships, or academic performance?

It generally just makes it really hard for me to keep up with things and stay organized in my day-to-day life. I can't really think of any specific examples right now, but it definitely feels like a constant struggle to stay on top of everything.

Can you estimate how often you complete tasks or reach your goals without significant difficulty or procrastination, and are there any situations where you feel more in control of your attention and focus?

I'm not really sure how often I succeed without a struggle, or which specific situations actually give me more control. It just feels like I almost always struggle with sustaining my attention on my tasks, no matter what I'm trying to do.
Do you experience any other symptoms such as depression, anxiety, or mood swings that could be contributing to your attention and focus difficulties?
No, I don't really experience depression, anxiety, or mood swings. My struggles are pretty much limited to the focus and distraction issues I mentioned earlier.
Are there any specific situations, activities, or environments where you notice your focus and distraction issues are significantly better or worse than usual?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed any specific environments or activities where my focus is significantly better or worse. It just seems to be a consistent struggle no matter where I am.
I'm sorry, doctor, I didn't catch that last part. Could you please repeat or clarify what you would like to know?
Can you think of any times when you're able to focus very well, such as when you're doing something you really enjoy, and if so, what is it about those situations that helps you stay focused?
I honestly can't really think of any times when I'm able to focus well. Even when I'm doing things I really enjoy, I still find myself getting easily distracted and struggling to pay attention.

Are you willing to try some strategies or treatments to help manage your focus and distraction issues, such as behavioral therapy, lifestyle changes, or medication, and do you have any questions or concerns about these potential treatments?
I'm definitely open to trying different strategies or treatments, but I'm not really sure which one would be the best option for me. What would you recommend we start with?
